images.title: Add 10 to every value, the mean moves 10
images.purpose: Shows that when every value goes up by 10 the mean also goes up by exactly 10.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two identical number lines stacked one above the other, a before dot plot on top and an after dot plot below, joined by one wide arrow on the right.
images.exact_structure: Two horizontal number lines, one above the other, both from 0 to 25 with 26 short tick marks, one per whole number, aligned exactly. Only the bottom line has numbers under it: 0, 10 and 20. Top line, teal (#0072B2) dots stacked in columns: 1 dot at 3, 1 at 4, 1 at 5, 1 at 6, 2 at 7, 3 at 8, 1 at 10, 1 at 13, which is 11 dots. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) triangle under the top line at 7.18, just right of 7, labelled mean about 7.18. Bottom line, amber (#E69F00) dots stacked the same way 10 to the right: 1 at 13, 1 at 14, 1 at 15, 1 at 16, 2 at 17, 3 at 18, 1 at 20, 1 at 23, which is 11 dots. A reddish purple triangle under the bottom line at 17.18, labelled mean about 17.18. One thick grey (#6B7280) arrow points down from the top plot to the bottom plot on the right side, labelled +10.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every dot moved 10 to the right, so the mean moved exactly 10 too.
images.description: Shows that when every value goes up by 10 the mean also goes up by exactly 10.
images.teaching_notes: The same picture works for doubling later; this image keeps only the shift.

image_decisions.why: A before and after dot plot makes the shift rule visible: every dot and the mean slide by the same 10.
